$comment: Machine-readable form of .security/POLICY.md - this file is what the gate
actually reads (.security/gate.py). POLICY.md explains and justifies it.
Keep the two in sync; the prose is the contract with humans, this is the

gitleaks.reason: A newly committed secret is never acceptable, whatever the rule's confidence. Rotate the credential, then rewrite history if it reached a shared branch.

pip-audit.reason: pip-audit emits no severity field at all, so severity filtering would silently drop every finding. Any new advisory blocks and must be triaged by hand.

trivy-fs.reason: Dependency and licence findings at MEDIUM and below are reported for visibility but do not block; the nightly run records the full distribution.

checkov.reason: Checkov community edition leaves severity null on every check, so severity filtering would silently drop every finding - the same problem as pip-audit. Checkov also only scans deploy/, which POLICY.md 3(b) treats as the security control rather than the vulnerable app, so a new finding there is a real finding and blocks.

trivy-config.reason: Same reasoning as checkov: the target is the pipeline's own infrastructure code, not the deliberately vulnerable application, so severity is the wrong filter for whether a new finding deserves attention.

conftest.reason: A conftest failure means deploy/k8s violates policy/kubernetes.rego - a policy this repository wrote about its own infrastructure. There is no severity to weigh and nothing to accept: the baseline for this scanner is expected to stay empty.
